run: mini-wallet — the complete Digital Credentials API channel against the raw Rust engine (all three module groups)

suite.variant: sd_jwt_vc / eudi_pid / dc_api.jwt / haip — all three request-method groups

wallet.profile: mini-wallet (wallet-frontend and go-wallet-backend disabled; the harness plays the browser's role — the engine's flow completes with the DigitalCredential's data and the spec hands it to the module's browser API submit URL, exactly as the suite's own page does)

engine_wire: The multi-signed request object (RFC 7515 §7.2, the JWS JSON Serialization): every signature verifies through its compact-equivalent against the x5c in its own protected header; at least one valid signature authenticates the verifier (one invalid is skipped — the module leaves the second valid on purpose); the client_id rides the signatures' protected headers, the first VERIFIED one's binding the wallet runs its scheme rules against

§5.9.2's bounds on the pre-registered fallback: an unknown-prefixed client_id names a pre-registered client only on an UNSIGNED request; a signed request's unknown prefix refuses, and a value embedding a recognized prefix can never be pre-registered
The web-origin form: a request with no client_id — the caller's origin IS the client (the transport's input fills it)
The origin binding is enforced for an authenticated verifier (a recognized Client Identifier Prefix or a signed request object); the unsigned pre-registered fallback's expected_origins is advisory
notes: REVIEW is the negative modules' expected outcome: the wallet refused each invalid request for the right reason, the browser API's promise rejection posted to the module's submit URL, and the tester's error-screen placeholder uploaded through the suite's API. Reproduce with: make wasm-page in siros-wallet-core, then npx playwright test specs/conformance/mini-wallet-vp-dcapi.spec.ts here (the spec runs all three groups).
